correctness.rationale: For each affine clipping mask, \(J=D+(I-D)P\) preserves constants. On a single-jump basis, the left values lie in \([0,\mu]\), right in \([\mu,1]\); summing \(j-1\) left edge bounds, \(n-j-1\) right edge bounds, and the bridge gives \(2j(n-j)/n\). Step decomposition and piecewise-affine path integration prove the global bound. Strictly feasible alternating masks plus arbitrarily small step perturbations attain equality, including all parity and one-clipped-site cases. The packaged rational checker exhausts masks for n=2..10 and strict attaining pairs for n=2..100; tests corroborate rather than prove the quantified all-n statement.

value.rationale: The exact natural two-input BV stability coefficient grows as half the data length even though the map individually diminishes variation, showing a significant instability of centered amplitude limiting. The theorem identifies the first expansive dimension (three), the exact parity correction, threshold-independence, and explicit attaining pairs. These are useful quantitative distinctions for variation-sensitive signal preprocessing and stability bounds, not merely a renamed scalar nonexpansivity inequality.
